englishTitle: Cockfight: Behind the Scenes of "The Drag Queens of New York"

authorship.author: Nimrod Dvir
authorship.classification: Nim-authored firsthand two-day set reporting with twelve interviewer statements

completenessChecks: 29 narrative/quotation paragraphs, 12 bold interviewer prompts and 2 section headings translated in original order; the source record counts 41 body blocks (paragraphs plus prompts) and 2 headings separately.
All 12 prompts kept bold and separate, including the interviewer's reply 'I'm on a break, and I don't want to steal the focus from the girls.' which has no question mark.
4 caption lines translated with PR credits.
Numbered points '1.' and '2.' kept as separate paragraphs as in the source.
No H1 added; no pull quote; opening and closing paragraphs complete.
voiceChecks: Opening 'Let's open with old news' and the hanging 'And still.' kept as the paragraph's last beat.
'Something of a coup.' kept as a fragment for 'סוג של שיחוק'.
Parenthetical asides retained ('if you can call them that', 'for example, that they are all looking for love', 'in this particular scene they used three').
Self-mockery kept: martinis and gawking; 'Look for my looks of astonishment when the episode airs.'
Interviewer's flat challenges ('Not exactly. With my own eyes I saw...') kept blunt, not softened.
Queens' speech kept at its own register (bitches, honey, sugar, darling) without smoothing.
decisions: Title: the Hebrew 'קרב תרנגולות' feminizes 'cockfight' (literally a hen fight); rendered as 'Cockfight' to match the verified APA gloss, with the nuance recorded here.
The show is named as Nim names it, 'The Drag Queens of New York'; the series was later broadcast under the title 'Queens of Drag: NYC', which the website version may want to note.

Hebrew series titles rendered with established English names: The Hills ('הוליווד הילס'), Keeping Up with the Kardashians ('משפחת קרדשיאן'), The Real Housewives, Desperate Housewives, The L Word ('ישנן בנות'), Project Runway.
Pnina Rosenblum glossed in three words ('Israel's cosmetics queen') because the joke depends on knowing her trade.

Drag names use their established English spellings (Hedda Lettuce, Sherry Vine, Bianca Del Rio, Mimi Imfurst, Acid Betty, Dallas DuBois); 'Mimi Imfurst' is the established spelling of the name Nim transliterates.
sourceProblems: Source was decoded from Windows-1255 despite a UTF-8 header; the Markdown text is clean.
One inline advertisement was removed during capture and the split text rejoined; no wording changed.
unresolvedQuestions: Whether to retitle 'Cockfight' as 'Catfight' for the website, which is the idiomatic English for the Hebrew pun, or keep the literal rendering.
